{{nihongo|'''Dewa Shrine'''|出羽神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Dewa Province]].

'''Dewa Shrine''' (いではじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located on the summit of {{ill|Mount Haguro|Q3090765|qid=Q3090765|lt=Mount Haguro}} in {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|Q125863|qid=Q125863}}. The enshrined deities are Ideha-no-Kami and {{ill|Ukanomitama|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|qid=Q3080728|lt=Inakura Tamano Mikoto}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} system it was classified as a {{ill|Q712534|lt=Kokuhei-shōsha}}.

=== Overview ===
{{ill|Dewa Province|Q876032|qid=Q876032}}’s southern region, the {{ill|Shōnai region|Q11485804|qid=Q11485804}} (the {{ill|Sea of Japan|Q27092|qid=Q27092}} side of Yamagata Prefecture), contains {{ill|Mount Gassan|Q3174863|qid=Q3174863}}, Mount Haguro, and {{ill|Mount Yudono|Q3322191|qid=Q3322191|lt=Mount Yudono}}. These are collectively known as the {{ill|Three Mountains of Dewa|Q1155726|qid=Q1155726}} and have long been objects of {{ill|Mountain worship|Q93697439|qid=Q93697439}}. Mount Haguro has served as one of the central sites of {{ill|Shugendō|Q1483875|qid=Q1483875}}, which developed through the {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088|lt=fusion}} of {{ill|Ko-Shintō|Q3096508|qid=Q3096508}} with {{ill|Buddhism|Q748|qid=Q748}} and other traditions.<ref>[http://www.dewasanzan.jp/publics/index/75/ Haguro School of Ancient Shugendō] Dewa Sanzan Shrine (accessed January 2, 2020)</ref>

Mount Haguro has 2,446 stone steps, and within the mountain precincts there is also a {{ill|Five-storied pagoda|Q11372713|qid=Q11372713}} (a {{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|Q1139795|qid=Q1139795}}).<ref name="日経20201212">[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO67152580Z01C20A2905W01/ No. 1: Dewa Sanzan Shrine (Yamagata Prefecture) — A serene and majestic space where Shinto and Buddhist deities dwell] {{ill|The Nikkei|Q1077694|qid=Q1077694}}, December 12, 2020, Saturday morning supplement NIKKEI Plus 1 “Anything Ranking” (front page), accessed January 2, 2021</ref>

The Three Mountains of Dewa are said to symbolize the past (Mount Gassan), the present (Mount Haguro), and the future (Mount Yudono),<ref name="日経20201212"/> and are respectively home to {{ill|Gassan Shrine|Q11516052|qid=Q11516052}}, Dewa Shrine, and {{ill|Yudonosan Shrine|Q11563607|qid=Q11563607}}. As a {{ill|religious corporation|Q7311343|qid=Q7311343}}, these three mountains are managed as a single corporation under the registered name “Gassan Shrine, Dewa Shrine, Yudonosan Shrine (Dewa Sanzan Shrine).” At Dewa Shrine on the summit of Mount Haguro stands the Sanjin Gōsaiden, which also houses the headquarters of the religious corporation. For cultural properties owned by the corporation, see “{{ill|Three Mountains of Dewa|Q1155726|qid=Q1155726}}.”
